project_dates_and_timing.name: project_dates_and_timing
project_dates_and_timing.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.unics_id,
  -- canonicalize start_date: use projects' start_date; if null, derive from start_year Jan 1; else null stays null
  COALESCE(
    p.start_date,
    CASE WHEN p.start_year IS NOT NULL THEN make_date(p.start_year, 1, 1) END
  ) AS start_date,
  -- canonicalize end_date: use projects' end_date; if null, derive from end_year Dec 31; else if both dates missing but start_date present assume start_date as end_date
  COALESCE(
    p.end_date,
    CASE WHEN p.end_year IS NOT NULL THEN make_date(p.end_year, 12, 31) END,
    -- fallback: if end_date & end_year missing but start_date known, treat project as 0-day duration (end = start)
    CASE WHEN p.end_date IS NULL AND p.end_year IS NULL AND COALESCE(p.start_date, (CASE WHEN p.start_year IS NOT NULL THEN make_date(p.start_year,1,1) END)) IS NOT NULL
         THEN COALESCE(p.start_date, (CASE WHEN p.start_year IS NOT NULL THEN make_date(p.start_year,1,1) END))
    END
  ) AS end_date,
  -- canonicalize start_year: prefer explicit field, else derive from start_date
  COALESCE(
    p.start_year,
    CASE WHEN p.start_date IS NOT NULL THEN extract(year from p.start_date)::integer END
  ) AS start_year,
  -- canonicalize end_year: prefer explicit field, else derive from end_date
  COALESCE(
    p.end_year,
    CASE WHEN p.end_date IS NOT NULL THEN extract(year from p.end_date)::integer END
  ) AS end_year,
  -- project_duration_days: difference in days between canonical end_date and canonical start_date (inclusive: +1), null if either boundary missing
  CASE
    WHEN
      COALESCE(
        p.start_date,
        CASE WHEN p.start_year IS NOT NULL THEN make_date(p.start_year, 1, 1) END
      ) IS NOT NULL
      AND
      COALESCE(
        p.end_date,
        CASE WHEN p.end_year IS NOT NULL THEN make_date(p.end_year, 12, 31) END,
        CASE WHEN p.end_date IS NULL AND p.end_year IS NULL AND COALESCE(p.start_date, (CASE WHEN p.start_year IS NOT NULL THEN make_date(p.start_year,1,1) END)) IS NOT NULL
             THEN COALESCE(p.start_date, (CASE WHEN p.start_year IS NOT NULL THEN make_date(p.start_year,1,1) END))
        END
      ) IS NOT NULL
    THEN
      -- compute inclusive day count
      (COALESCE(
        p.end_date,
        CASE WHEN p.end_year IS NOT NULL THEN make_date(p.end_year, 12, 31) END,
        CASE WHEN p.end_date IS NULL AND p.end_year IS NULL AND COALESCE(p.start_date, (CASE WHEN p.start_year IS NOT NULL THEN make_date(p.start_year,1,1) END)) IS NOT NULL
             THEN COALESCE(p.start_date, (CASE WHEN p.start_year IS NOT NULL THEN make_date(p.start_year,1,1) END))
        END
      )::date
      - COALESCE(
        p.start_date,
        CASE WHEN p.start_year IS NOT NULL THEN make_date(p.start_year, 1, 1) END
      )::date
      ) + 1
    ELSE NULL
  END AS project_duration_days
FROM projects_row_level p
project_dates_and_timing.description: Normalized project date and year fields with explicit canonical date boundaries and derived duration measure; one row per project.

SELECT

  i.institutions_name  AS institutions_name,
  pm.country           AS country,
  pm.member_role       AS member_role,
  pm.ec_contribution   AS ec_contribution,
  COALESCE(pm.geocode_regions_3, i.geocode_regions_3) AS geocode_regions_3
FROM
  project_members pm
LEFT JOIN
  institutions i
ON
  pm.institution_id = i.unics_id
project_membership_w_institutions.description: Denormalized project-member rows joined to institution metadata to enable questions that relate projects to participating institutions, member roles, country and geocode regions.

projects_with_programme_and_topics.name: projects_with_programme_and_topics
projects_with_programme_and_topics.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.unics_id AS project_unics_id,
  pp.programme AS programme,
  psa.subject_area AS subject_area,
  pt.topic AS topic
FROM projects p
-- left join to programme if present
LEFT JOIN project_programmes pp
  ON pp.project = p.unics_id
-- left join to subject areas (may be null)
LEFT JOIN project_subject_areas psa
  ON psa.project = p.unics_id
-- left join to topics (may be null)
LEFT JOIN project_topics pt
  ON pt.project = p.unics_id
-- Ensure we return a row when either a subject_area or a topic exists (or even neither, keeping project-level row)
-- No additional filtering here; consumers can filter by programme, subject_area or topic as needed.
projects_with_programme_and_topics.description: Project-level denormalized view exposing project id with associated programme code, subject areas and topics (one row per project-topic or project-subject depending on presence). Useful for filtering projects by programme, topic or subject area.

institutions_core.name: institutions_core
institutions_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- canonical display name for the institution
  coalesce(institutions.institutions_name, '') AS institutions_name,
  -- primary key carried through
  institutions.unics_id,
  -- country id as stored on institutions table (nullable)
  institutions.country_id,
  -- canonical 3-region geocode (use institutions value if present)
  NULLIF(trim(coalesce(institutions.geocode_regions_3, '')), '') AS geocode_regions_3,
  -- region name: prefer institution's region_name if present via a join to countries by country_id,
  -- else NULL. Keep as text.
  countries.country_name AS region_name
FROM institutions
LEFT JOIN countries
  ON institutions.country_id = countries.unics_id
institutions_core.description: Canonical row-level view of institutions with core identifying and geographic columns, cleaned/canonicalized for downstream filtering and joins.

project_members_core.name: project_members_core
project_members_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  pm.unics_id::integer AS unics_id,
  pm.project::integer AS project,
  -- keep institution_id as integer, NULLs preserved
  pm.institution_id::integer AS institution_id,
  -- trim whitespace from names
  trim(pm.member_name) AS member_name,
  -- normalize country to upper-case ISO-like code where provided; lift literal for default behavior
  nullif(trim(pm.country), '')::text AS country,
  -- ensure contribution is numeric, keep NULL if absent
  pm.ec_contribution::double precision AS ec_contribution,
  -- normalize role to lower-case short code where available; keep original otherwise
  nullif(trim(pm.member_role), '') AS member_role,
  nullif(trim(pm.member_short_name), '') AS member_short_name,
  -- latitude/longitude as numeric; preserve scale
  pm.latitude::numeric AS latitude,
  pm.longitude::numeric AS longitude
FROM
  project_members pm
project_members_core.description: One row per project_member exposing membership links to project, institution, country and financial contribution. Clean/normalize key columns used for joins and filters.

institutions_core_30.name: institutions_core_30
institutions_core_30.body_sql:
SELECT
  institutions_name,
  unics_id,
  country_id,
  geocode_regions_3,
  -- provide a cleaned short_name: prefer explicit short_name, fall back to institutions_name truncated
  NULLIF(trim(short_name), '') AS short_name,
  -- normalized acronym: empty string -> null, trim whitespace and upper-case for consistency
  NULLIF(trim(acronym), '') AS acronym,
  -- ensure website is a trimmed http(s) URL where possible; otherwise NULL
  CASE
    WHEN website IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN trim(website) = '' THEN NULL
    ELSE
      -- simple normalization: if missing scheme, prefix 'http://' ; keep as-is otherwise
      CASE
        WHEN website ~* '^\s*https?://' THEN trim(website)
        ELSE 'http://' || trim(website)
      END
  END AS website
FROM institutions
institutions_core_30.description: Canonical institution rows with key identifiers and cleaned contact/location fields; preserves one row per institution for reuse in filtering, joining, and projection.

FROM projects p
projects_financial_measures.description: Aggregated financial measures per project. Produces one row per project with key monetary fields preserved for comparisons and ranking.

project_members_row_level.name: project_members_row_level
project_members_row_level.body_sql:
SELECT
  pm.unics_id,
  pm.project,
  -- preserve member_name as-is (NULL kept when absent)
  pm.member_name,
  pm.member_short_name,
  pm.member_role,
  pm.institution_id,
  pm.ec_contribution,
  pm.country,
  pm.city,
  pm.postal_code,
  pm.latitude,
  pm.longitude,
  pm.geocode_regions_3
FROM project_members pm
project_members_row_level.description: One row per project-member relation exposing member identity, role, institution link and location/cost contribution fields; preserves member_name only when present (NULL kept otherwise) so caller can filter for non-null names.

project_member_rows.name: project_member_rows
project_member_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  pm.unics_id AS "project_members.unics_id",
  pm.project AS "project_members.project",
  pm.institution_id AS "project_members.institution_id",
  pm.member_name AS "project_members.member_name",
  pm.activity_type AS "project_members.activity_type"
FROM
  project_members pm
project_member_rows.description: Row-level cohort of project members. One row per project_members record, exposing project id and member-level attributes useful for counting or filtering.

projects_basic.name: projects_basic
projects_basic.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.unics_id                                                   AS "projects.unics_id",
  p.acronym                                                    AS "projects.acronym",
  p.title                                                      AS "projects.title",
  p.start_year                                                 AS "projects.start_year",
  p.end_year                                                   AS "projects.end_year"
FROM
  projects p
projects_basic.description: Canonical project rows exposing primary identifiers and key metadata for joins (no filtering).

member_counts_per_project.name: member_counts_per_project
member_counts_per_project.body_sql:
SELECT
  pm.project AS project,
  count(*)::bigint AS member_count
FROM
  project_members pm
GROUP BY
  pm.project
member_counts_per_project.description: Aggregate count of project_members per project (one row per project id) to support queries that filter projects by member counts.

funding_schemes_dim.name: funding_schemes_dim
funding_schemes_dim.body_sql:
SELECT
  fs.code AS code,
  fs.title AS title
FROM funding_schemes fs
funding_schemes_dim.description: Canonical dimension table for funding schemes exposing scheme code and human-readable title.
validated_on: Find the code of the funding scheme for Framework Partnership Agreement

projects_by_funding_scheme.name: projects_by_funding_scheme
projects_by_funding_scheme.body_sql:
SELECT
  pc.ec_fund_scheme,
  COUNT(*) AS project_count
FROM (
  SELECT unics_id, ec_fund_scheme
  FROM projects
) AS pc
GROUP BY pc.ec_fund_scheme
projects_by_funding_scheme.description: Pre-aggregated counts of projects per funding scheme code (one row per funding scheme code). NULL scheme codes are included as a row with ec_fund_scheme = NULL unless filtered out by the question.

project_financials_by_project.name: project_financials_by_project
project_financials_by_project.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.unics_id,
  COALESCE(SUM(p.total_cost), 0.0) AS total_cost_sum,
  COALESCE(SUM(p.ec_max_contribution), 0.0) AS ec_max_contribution_sum
FROM projects AS p
GROUP BY p.unics_id
project_financials_by_project.description: Per-project financial measures. Aggregates any duplicate project rows (if present) by summing monetary fields per project id. Exposes raw measures for downstream grouping/filtering.

projects_with_program_and_pi.name: projects_with_program_and_pi
projects_with_program_and_pi.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.unics_id,
  p.acronym,
  p.title,
  p.total_cost,
  p.framework_program,
  ep.ec_framework_program_name AS programme_title,
  p.principal_investigator,
  pe.full_name AS pi_full_name
FROM projects p
LEFT JOIN ec_framework_programs ep
  ON p.framework_program = ep.ec_framework_program_name
LEFT JOIN people pe
  ON p.principal_investigator = pe.unics_id
projects_with_program_and_pi.description: Denormalized project rows joined to programme code/title and principal investigator person name where available. One row per project; useful when filtering or grouping by programme or PI.

project_members_by_project.name: project_members_by_project
project_members_by_project.body_sql:
SELECT
  pm.unics_id                                  AS project,
  pm.member_name                               AS member_name,
  pm.institution_id                            AS institution_id,
  pm.ec_contribution                           AS ec_contribution,
  pm.country                                   AS country,
  pm.region_code                               AS region_code,
  pm.geocode_regions_3                         AS geocode_regions_3
FROM project_members pm
project_members_by_project.description: Denormalized membership rows linking projects to their members and member institutions, exposing contribution and geographic columns useful for filtering/aggregation by project.

institutions_core_43.name: institutions_core_43
institutions_core_43.body_sql:
SELECT
  unics_id,
  institutions_name,
  short_name,
  acronym,
  country_id,
  geocode_regions_3,
  website,
  grid_id
FROM institutions
institutions_core_43.description: Canonical projection of institutions exposing identifiers, country and region geocodes, and common name/acronym fields for joins and geographic filtering.

projects_with_years.name: projects_with_years
projects_with_years.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.unics_id,
  p.acronym,
  p.title,
  p.start_year,
  p.end_year,
  /* duration_years: difference between end_year and start_year when both present */
  CASE
    WHEN p.start_year IS NOT NULL AND p.end_year IS NOT NULL THEN (p.end_year - p.start_year)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS duration_years
FROM projects_row_level p
projects_with_years.description: One row per project exposing its identifiers, title, start and end year and basic timeline measures; filters for non-null years are left to question_ops.

projects_with_topics.name: projects_with_topics
projects_with_topics.body_sql:
SELECT
  pt.project AS project,
  pt.topic AS topic,
  p.unics_id AS "projects.unics_id",
  p.title AS "projects.title",
  p.start_year AS "projects.start_year",
  p.end_year AS "projects.end_year"
FROM
  project_topics pt
JOIN
  projects p
    ON pt.project = p.unics_id
projects_with_topics.description: Denormalized relation linking projects to their topics, exposing project and topic ids and project title/year for filtering and aggregation across project-topic associations.

topic_titles_search_cohort.name: topic_titles_search_cohort
topic_titles_search_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.code AS code,
  t.title AS title
FROM topics t
topic_titles_search_cohort.description: Search-focused subset of topics exposing titles for fast LIKE/starts-with matching and retrieval; keeps one row per topic code.

topics_text.name: topics_text
topics_text.body_sql:
SELECT
  code,
  -- normalized/cleaned title suitable for text filtering/searching.
  -- Lift question-specific literals out: here none needed.
  -- Trim whitespace and collapse internal spaces, and lower-case for normalization.
  trim(regexp_replace(coalesce(title, ''), '\s+', ' ', 'g')) AS title
FROM topics
topics_text.description: Normalized projection of the topics table exposing topic id and cleaned title for text filtering and searching.

topics_for_search_cohort.name: topics_for_search_cohort
topics_for_search_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.code AS code,
  t.title AS title
FROM topics t
WHERE t.title IS NOT NULL
topics_for_search_cohort.description: A reusable selectable cohort of topic rows with non-null titles suitable for substring or full-text queries. Keeps one row per topic and exposes the title for pattern matching.

project_with_principal_investigator.name: project_with_principal_investigator
project_with_principal_investigator.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.unics_id                                    AS "projects.unics_id",
  p.principal_investigator                      AS "projects.principal_investigator",
  pe.full_name                                  AS "people.full_name",
  p.title                                       AS "projects.title",
  p.start_date                                  AS "projects.start_date",
  p.end_date                                    AS "projects.end_date"
FROM projects p
LEFT JOIN people pe
  ON p.principal_investigator = pe.unics_id
project_with_principal_investigator.description: Denormalized row-level view joining projects to people on the principal investigator foreign key, so each row is a project with the PI's person id and name. Useful for queries that filter or aggregate projects by PI attributes.

people_non_null_names.name: people_non_null_names
people_non_null_names.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.unics_id,
  p.full_name
FROM
  people p
WHERE
  p.full_name IS NOT NULL
people_non_null_names.description: Subset of people where a full_name is present. Useful as a ready cohort when queries need only persons with names.

project_financials_cohort.name: project_financials_cohort
project_financials_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.unics_id AS unics_id,
  p.acronym AS acronym,
  p.total_cost AS total_cost,
  p.ec_max_contribution AS ec_max_contribution,
  p.start_date AS start_date,
  p.end_date AS end_date,
  p.start_year AS start_year,
  p.end_year AS end_year
FROM projects p
project_financials_cohort.description: Cohort of projects with key financial measures and date fields used for monetary and temporal filters. Useful for questions that filter or aggregate by project cost or timeframe.

project_membership_wide.name: project_membership_wide
project_membership_wide.body_sql:
SELECT
  pm.project AS project,
  pm.unics_id AS "project_members.unics_id",
  pm.member_name AS member_name,
  pm.institution_id AS institution_id,
  pm.member_role AS member_role,
  pm.ec_contribution AS ec_contribution,
  pm.country AS country,
  pm.region_code AS region_code,
  pm.geocode_regions_3 AS geocode_regions_3
FROM project_members pm
project_membership_wide.description: Denormalized row per project-member linking projects to participating institution/member info and their financial contribution. Exposes project id, member id, member role, institution id and ec_contribution for queries that join project attributes with member-level contributions or geography.

projects_row_level_53.name: projects_row_level_53
projects_row_level_53.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.unics_id,
  p.title,
  p.start_date,
  p.end_date,
  p.start_year,
  p.end_year,
  p.total_cost,
  p.ec_max_contribution,
  p.framework_program,
  p.principal_investigator
FROM projects AS p
projects_row_level_53.description: Row-level canonical projection of projects exposing identifying keys and core numeric measures for filtering and aggregation.

project_with_principal_investigator_and_.name: project_with_principal_investigator_and_institution
project_with_principal_investigator_and_.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.unics_id AS unics_id,
  p.title AS title,
  p.principal_investigator AS principal_investigator,
  pe.full_name AS pi_full_name,
  pm.institution_id AS institution_id,
  pm.member_name AS member_name,
  i.institutions_name AS institutions_name,
  i.country_id AS country_id
FROM projects p
LEFT JOIN people pe
  ON p.principal_investigator = pe.unics_id
LEFT JOIN project_members pm
  ON p.unics_id = pm.project
LEFT JOIN institutions i
  ON pm.institution_id = i.unics_id
project_with_principal_investigator_and_.description: Denormalized view joining projects to principal investigator (person) and to institution info via project.principal_investigator -> people.unics_id and project_members/institutions where available. Exposes project title, project id, principal investigator id and name, and institution id/name for queries that need human/institutional context.

project_members_partner_cohort.name: project_members_partner_cohort
project_members_partner_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  pm.project,
  pm.member_name,
  pm.member_role,
  pm.institution_id,
  pm.unics_id AS "project_members.unics_id"
FROM project_members pm
WHERE pm.member_role IS NOT NULL
  AND pm.member_role ~* 'partner'
project_members_partner_cohort.description: Cohort of project_members rows that have a non-null member_role and whose role text indicates a partner role (case-insensitive match). Keep one row per project_member record.

project_with_partner_members.name: project_with_partner_members
project_with_partner_members.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.title AS project_title,
  p.unics_id AS project_unics_id,
  pm.member_name AS member_name,
  pm.member_role AS member_role,
  pm.unics_id AS member_unics_id,
  pm.institution_id AS institution_id
FROM project_members pm
JOIN projects p
  ON pm.project = p.unics_id
WHERE pm.member_role IS NOT NULL
  AND pm.member_role <> ''
  -- Lift question-specific literals out: treat non-empty member_role as partner indicator
project_with_partner_members.description: Denormalized join of projects to their member rows that appear to be partners. One row per partner member of a project.

erc_research_domains_core.name: erc_research_domains_core
erc_research_domains_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  rr.code::text AS code,
  NULLIF(btrim(regexp_replace(rr.description::text, '\s+', ' ', 'g')), '') AS description
FROM erc_research_domains rr
erc_research_domains_core.description: Canonical projection of ERC research domain codes and descriptions (one row per research domain). Cleans/canonicalizes text but does not filter or aggregate.

institutions_with_country_name.name: institutions_with_country_name
institutions_with_country_name.body_sql:
SELECT
  i.unics_id,
  i.institutions_name,
  i.country_id,
  c.country_name
FROM institutions i
LEFT JOIN countries c
  ON i.country_id = c.unics_id
institutions_with_country_name.description: Denormalized view: one row per institution with the linked country_name (NULL when no matching country). Useful for queries that list institutions with their country names.

institutions_with_country_59.name: institutions_with_country_59
institutions_with_country_59.body_sql:
SELECT
  institutions.unics_id AS institution_id,
  institutions.institutions_name AS institution_name,
  countries.country_name AS country_name,
  countries.unics_id AS country_unics_id
FROM institutions
LEFT JOIN countries
  ON institutions.country_id = countries.unics_id
institutions_with_country_59.description: One-row-per-institution with its linked country fields; denormalizes institutions joined to countries to expose institution and country identifiers and names for filtering, grouping and display.

institutions_core_60.name: institutions_core_60
institutions_core_60.body_sql:
SELECT
  unics_id AS institution_id,
  institutions_name AS institution_name,
  country_id,
  geocode_regions_3,
  acronym,
  short_name,
  website
FROM institutions
institutions_core_60.description: Canonical projection of institutions exposing primary identifiers and common location/geocode columns for downstream joins and filtering. Keeps one row per institution and normalizes column names for reuse.

countries_core.name: countries_core
countries_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  unics_id AS country_unics_id,
  country_name,
  country_code2,
  country_code3,
  geocode_country_code
FROM countries
countries_core.description: Canonical projection of countries exposing primary key and common name/code columns for joins and display.

countries_by_name.name: countries_by_name
countries_by_name.body_sql:
SELECT
  country_name,
  country_code2,
  country_code3,
  unics_id
FROM countries
countries_by_name.description: Selectable cohort of countries including key name and codes to allow name-based lookups and canonical joins; useful for answering questions that filter by country_name.

funding_schemes_search_text.name: funding_schemes_search_text
funding_schemes_search_text.body_sql:
SELECT
  fs.code AS code,
  fs.title AS title,
  -- normalized title: lowercased, trimmed, internal whitespace collapsed to single space
  regexp_replace(lower(trim(fs.title)), '\s+', ' ', 'g') AS title_normalized
FROM funding_schemes fs
funding_schemes_search_text.description: Canonicalized text forms for funding_schemes.title to support case-insensitive and trimmed comparisons and simple search; keeps one row per funding scheme.

programmes_core.name: programmes_core
programmes_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  code::text AS code,
  rcn::text AS rcn,
  title::text AS title,
  short_name::text AS short_name,
  parent::text AS parent
FROM programmes
programmes_core.description: Canonical cleaned projection of programmes table exposing programme identifiers, names, titles and parent relationship. Suitable as the base for lookups by code, rcn, short_name or title.

programmes_by_shortname_lookup.name: programmes_by_shortname_lookup
programmes_by_shortname_lookup.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.code AS code,
  p.short_name AS short_name,
  p.title AS title,
  p.rcn AS rcn
FROM programmes p
programmes_by_shortname_lookup.description: Subset/cohort view of programmes exposing programmes keyed by short_name to support direct short_name-based lookup and possible disambiguation when multiple programmes share the same short_name.

project_members_core_66.name: project_members_core_66
project_members_core_66.body_sql:
SELECT
  pm.unics_id,
  pm.project,
  pm.member_name,
  pm.member_role,
  pm.institution_id,
  pm.activity_type,
  pm.country,
  pm.ec_contribution,
  pm.latitude,
  pm.longitude,
  pm.member_short_name
FROM project_members pm
project_members_core_66.description: Row-level cohort of project members with core identifying and contact fields. Each row represents one project_member record.

project_members_with_project.name: project_members_with_project
project_members_with_project.body_sql:
SELECT
  pm.unics_id AS unics_id,
  pm.project AS project,
  pm.member_name AS member_name,
  pm.member_role AS member_role,
  p.acronym AS project_acronym,
  p.title AS project_title,
  p.start_year AS project_start_year,
  p.end_year AS project_end_year
FROM project_members pm
JOIN projects p
  ON pm.project = p.unics_id
project_members_with_project.description: Denormalized view joining project_members to projects so queries can filter by project attributes (e.g., acronym) while keeping one row per project member.
